oe_iac.description: Infrastructure and deployments are defined as code / automated, not manual console changes.

oe_observability.description: Monitoring, logging, and alerting are defined for the workload's key operational signals.

oe_incident_response.description: An incident response process or runbook is referenced for operational failures.

oe_change_mgmt.description: Changes can be rolled back safely; deployment approach limits blast radius of a bad change.

sec_least_privilege.description: IAM roles/permissions follow least privilege rather than broad/wildcard access.

sec_encryption_at_rest.description: Sensitive or PII-bearing data stores have encryption at rest specified.

sec_encryption_transit.description: Data in transit is encrypted (TLS) between components, especially over public networks.

sec_secrets_mgmt.description: Credentials/API keys/secrets are managed via a secrets store, not hardcoded or embedded in config.

sec_network_perimeter.description: Network boundaries/segmentation are defined; public-facing components are minimized and fronted appropriately.

sec_identity_auth.description: Authentication/authorization (SSO, MFA, RBAC) is defined for user- and system-facing access.

sec_audit_logging.description: Security-relevant actions and access are logged in an auditable, tamper-resistant way.

rel_redundancy.description: Critical components have redundancy (multi-AZ or equivalent) rather than a single point of failure.

rel_dr_plan.description: A disaster recovery approach with defined RTO/RPO is present for critical data/workloads.

rel_failure_isolation.description: Dependent-service failures are isolated (retries, timeouts, circuit breakers, dead-letter queues) rather than cascading.

rel_backup.description: A backup strategy exists for stateful data with a defined restore process.

perf_right_sizing.description: Compute/storage choices match the actual workload pattern (e.g., serverless for spiky load) rather than over-provisioning.

perf_caching.description: Caching is used where repeated reads or expensive computations would otherwise recur.

perf_data_store_fit.description: The database/storage type matches its access pattern (e.g., not using a relational store for pure key-value lookups at scale).

perf_global_delivery.description: Content/data delivery accounts for geographic distribution of users where relevant (CDN or regional deployment).

cost_visibility.description: Cost tracking/tagging/budgets are defined so spend is attributable and boundable.

cost_elasticity.description: Resources scale down/to zero with demand rather than running at fixed capacity for variable load.

cost_storage_lifecycle.description: Storage has a lifecycle/retention policy rather than indefinite accumulation at full-cost tiers.

cost_provisioning_model.description: Provisioning model (on-demand vs reserved/provisioned) matches the workload's actual usage predictability.

sus_managed_services.description: Managed/serverless services are used where feasible to improve utilization over self-managed idle infrastructure.

sus_data_minimization.description: Data retention/storage footprint is minimized to what's needed rather than retained indefinitely by default.

sus_region_awareness.description: Region/deployment choice shows awareness of energy/carbon considerations where it doesn't conflict with other constraints.

tf_explainability.description: AI-driven decisions that affect people can be explained at a level appropriate to the audience.

tf_fairness.description: AI outputs are evaluated for unjustified variation across populations/segments where the use case involves consequential decisions.

tf_hallucination_control.description: LLM outputs are grounded (RAG, validation, citation) rather than relying on unverified generation for factual claims.

tf_privacy.description: PII flowing through AI components is identified and protected (minimization, masking, or encryption).

rr_ai_threat_model.description: AI-specific threats (prompt injection, data poisoning, model extraction) are considered, not just traditional infra security.

rr_incident_response_ai.description: An incident response path exists specifically for AI failures (bad output, hallucination, misuse), not just general system incidents.

rr_validation_before_prod.description: AI models/outputs are validated (testing, red-teaming, or human review) before being relied upon in production.

ue_cost_per_unit.description: Cost per AI call/decision is knowable or estimable, not opaque.

ue_model_routing.description: Cheaper/smaller models are used for simple tasks, reserving expensive models for tasks that need them.

ue_caching_ai.description: Repeated or semantically similar AI queries are cached rather than always re-invoking the model.

ss_data_residency.description: Data residency/location constraints are explicit and enforced by design, not left implicit.

ss_provider_dependency.description: Foundation model/vendor dependency is acknowledged with some consideration of switching cost or exit path.

ss_abstraction.description: AI provider calls are abstracted behind an internal interface rather than tightly coupled to one vendor's SDK throughout the codebase.

ta_human_in_loop.description: Consequential AI decisions retain a human review/override point rather than being fully autonomous.

ta_user_training.description: End users/operators have a defined path to understand and correctly use the AI system's outputs.

sai_inference_efficiency.description: Design choices (model size, caching, batching) that reduce cost also incidentally reduce AI inference energy footprint.

gov_model_inventory.description: Each AI model/component in the design has a clear named owner and purpose.

gov_audit_trail.description: AI decisions/outputs are logged with enough context (input, model version, output) to be reconstructed later.

gov_accountability.description: It's clear who is accountable when the AI produces an incorrect or harmful output.
